page: Microsoft Azure E48as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz, providing 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local temporary storage is bundled via an 825 GB SSD. No physical GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute capabilities alongside mid-range single-thread execution. The instance achieved top-quartile results in multi-core metrics, including 64,919.46 on stress-ng multi-core, a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,937.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 51,680.81. Cryptographic and compression pipelines benefit from dedicated hardware instructions, showing top 25% performance in PassMark CPU encryption (51,516.84) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (224.67 GB/sec). Memory benchmarks reflect solid aggregate throughput, scoring 2,969.9 in PassMark memory testing, 109.15 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads, and 59.9 GB/sec on writes.

Instruction set features support base AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, but lack AVX-512 extensions and AMX matrix instructions. This restriction shapes its machine learning profile: while text generation on small 135M parameter LLMs reaches the top 25% at 275.91 tokens/sec, large-scale execution lags, with 70B parameter text generation falling to the bottom 25% at 2.66 tokens/sec.

In operational database and storage benchmarks, the E48as_v4 handled 46.96 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved 19,812.35 on PassMark database operations, placing it in the middle tier. The large memory capacity combined with dedicated multi-core throughput makes the E48as_v4 suitable for large in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, batch data processing, and memory-intensive analytics workloads.

It provides 384.0 GB of memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes an 825 GB local SSD with zero bundled GPUs. Benchmark performance highlights strong multi-core processing, recording top-quartile results in stress-ng multi-core (64,919.46), Geekbench multi-core (15,937.0), PassMark CPU score (51,680.81), and PassMark CPU encryption (51,516.84). The instance exhibits mid-range memory bandwidth with 109.15 GB/sec uncached reads and average single-thread performance. The lack of AVX-512 caps large-model LLM generation speeds. Given its 384 GB footprint and multi-threaded throughput, the E48as_v4 is best aligned with large in-memory caching platforms, relational databases, data warehousing, and memory-intensive analytics.
